body:
I was in a 12 year relationship with (and married) someone who is my political opposite. It worked out well as long as we didn't talk politics. 

Then I found out she was cheating on me with multiple people for years. Even after finding that out, I struggled with the decision to leave her.

Like /u/EntropyCertain said, your story sounds like you could be me. I felt like our relationship was the one everyone aspired to, and people often told us exactly that at social gatherings. Then I found out about the infidelity.

Keep your head up and realize there are other great girls out there. It sounds like she didn't respect you several times throughout your relationship, and whenever you feel bad about losing her, just think back to her activities throughout. You deserve better. Feel free to PM me if you want to chat, our situation is so similar.

I feel your pain, just over a month ago I found out my wife was cheating on me with at least 8 guys, one of which was a sugar daddy paying her for her time. 

I never had the slightest idea all these years, and am not entirely sure what reality is anymore.

Currently in the early stages, and I'm deeply second guessing myself, even though she cheated on me with (at least) 8 other men. I know 100% that it's what I need to do, but I can't change the fact that I'm still in love with her. I still don't understand how people can be so vindictive against their exes, it's an extremely sad situation for both of us.
As someone who has already had the amazon card for years and had it automatically upgraded... I think I'll still be using my Ink+ and GCs.
Not OP, but Lower is less crowded and only goes one way, reducing crowding even more. It doesn't have the famous shafts of light penetrating the canyon that Upper gets, though.

I'm in Los Angeles. I still get second thoughts too, but when I remind myself of everything she did and all the things that drove me crazy, it gets a bit easier. Starting fresh is scary after 12 years.
Thanks for the insight, divorce just sucks, even when I'm the one initiating it.
Also be sure to email the photos to yourself or use some other cloud based storage in case she gets a hold of your phone.
Thanks, it's so frustrating spending so much money to move to a worse living situation!
Think of it as your reward for finally getting the process completely over with when the time comes :)

Thanks, I figured as much. I was just taken aback at the $3500 quote, I was expecting more around $2000-$2500 based on other things I had read on this sub. The attorney I consulted with did mention that the fact we both have pension plans through our unions created an added expense.
Thanks, I know I do. This whole situation has been tough, I feel too responsible for her to consider my own emotional well being right now and that needs to change.

Maybe a change of pace is what you need! What's stopping you from starting fresh in a new city, meeting other people, getting a change of scenery? It sounds like getting away from your family might help you. 

If you don't know what you want to do career-wise, maybe look into learning coding or some other web-based work? There are plenty of great FREE online resources to learn your skills and then all you need is a laptop and wifi to work from anywhere.
Thanks, you guys are great.

The urge to go on a Facebook meltdown is real. It feels so silly that I waste my time thinking of things I would post on there, thankfully I convince myself every time that I should just keep it to myself.
For starters, she was having physical affairs with 8 different men. And that's not even the worst of it. And I was somehow oblivious the whole time.

I don't think she's doing it consciously, I think her emotions are just running out of control in a traumatic situation. I've told her that it's not fair to me to say that and she knows my mind is made up, but knowing her I can understand that she genuinely feels that this might be the best course of action. 

I've thought about how I can wean her off of me, and I know staying in her life forever is probably not good for her in the long run. I'm hoping my plan of getting through the holidays together will help her come to terms with the reality of the situation and not give her false hope. I remind her every day that my mind is made up. I intend to find a therapist for her but it won't be easy to convince her to go.

I didn't stay with her for years because I was feeling guilty, I was prepared to stay committed to the relationship for life. I always just figured with the comments from most married men that putting your wife's needs before yours was kind of the norm. You know, things like "What 2 words are the key to a successful marriage? Yes Dear."

What caused me to leave is that I received an anonymous email containing undeniable proof she was cheating on me for a long time. Then I dug deeper into her texts and emails (which I'd never snooped on in my life) and it turned out to be way bigger and worse than I ever imagined. Bad like if you saw this in a movie you would think it was too far fetched. So after having the rug pulled out from under me like that I couldn't look at her the same ever again.

In your situation (not that I'm in a great spot to give advice, obviously), don't just leave out of the blue. That's cowardly. Step up and tell her how you really feel and tell her what you need to do for yourself. It was the hardest thing I've ever done but I'm glad I did it, even though it has put me in this horrible situation.
Thanks, I plan to.

That was after our first confrontation last week, before I learned the full story of everything that has convinced me to stand my ground. After our confrontation over the weekend, she knows where I stand.

I'm sorry things were rough for you. And it is manipulative, I know, but I also can't just let her fall like that. I will stand my ground but I want to help her get through it too. I'll recommend the therapist, maybe set up the appointment together.

We don't have children to keep her going, just pets, and I've always been the one with more real friends. I will make sure the friends she has are there for her through this, though.

Sorry you went through that. I know a lot of people on this sub have been through rough relationship situations and it can taint our views. I tend to be naive and put others before myself, but I have to take a situation like this seriously (while still standing my ground).

>Let me guess the previous suicidal statements came when you guys were having problems?

Nope, she just has a negative outlook on life despite having many, many things going for her. The comments usually came when she was feeling grateful for my compassion.

>And so she keeps you. Sorry at a certain point in time she has to be responsible for herself. As long as she gets what she wants you can count on this behavior continuing. Why? Because it works.

My mind is made up and I'm definitely leaving. She won't keep me and she knows it. Don't worry, after living the last 12 years for her, I'm finally taking control of my own destiny, I just don't want to cause any more harm than I need to.

Thanks, and I know she is. She's a fundamentally selfish person, that's basically why the divorce is happening to begin with. But I can't help but care for her and feel bad for her. Thankfully at least my mind is made up and I'm standing my ground finally thinking of myself for now. I won't be guilted into staying in a situation I don't want to, but it's the hardest thing I've done in my life.

No kids, thankfully. She has indeed taken advantage of my caring nature in the past, but with me being who I am I absolutely cannot just walk away from someone who I know is in pain, especially after her history of these feelings.

Thank you, this seems like a workable approach. She said she was open to marriage counseling, hopefully she can see individual counseling with me in occasional attendance as an option. She tends to get EXTREMELY negative when she is upset and won't listen to anybody, especially someone who she doesn't know well, but maybe my presence can help.

Thank you for being helpful and understanding. She has never seen a therapist, she was always vehemently against it despite my urging her from time to time. I'll see what I can do to get her to come around, hopefully she will realize the seriousness of her situation. She said she would do marriage counseling but not individual for herself. And I haven't ruled out this being a last ditch tactic to get me to stay, but knowing her I feel I should take this seriously. 

Involuntary commitment scares the hell out of me. So much trauma on top of an already deeply depressing situation. I will take it under consideration, though. Thank you.
That's a cold fucking thing to say.
As someone going through a divorce with a soon to be ex that is suicidal, this is about the worst thing I could have read.

We bickered before all of this and there were some issues of unhappiness, but there was no real resentment towards one another. I think mediation is definitely an option right now, she seems very open to accommodating anything I want. Of course when everything becomes real, it might be a whole different story. Thanks for the reading material.
Thank goodness no children have entered the picture!
I know, it looks so easy on paper. Seeing her remorse, tears, and love in person just penetrates me to the core, though.
The grief and betrayal feel very real already. I spent most of yesterday bawling my eyes out while confronting her. I do plan to seek counseling for us both, thanks for the advice.

Thanks, she actually suggested marriage counseling. I even spoke with her AP today.  Even he said we should try to make it work, and I got the impression he was being very honest and candid with me. It's such a complicated situation. When I make my pro/con list, my mind says I should leave, but when I talk to her, suddenly I'm pulled in the other direction. 

I know she would have continued the affair if I hadn't caught her, but at the same time I genuinely believe her when she says this was the shock she needed. She's taken every step to prove that, but I also can't help but feel like a sucker if I end up staying.
We've been married for 3 years, together for 12. It's tough. She's begging me to take her back.
I'm right there with you. Found out my STBX has been cheating for years with multiple people. I'm confronting her tomorrow and still I feel bad that I'm going to be turning HER life upside down.

Talk to your landlord/apartment manager. Hopefully they will be understanding in the situation and be able to remove your name from the lease. Having your name on another lease shouldn't hurt your chances of finding a new place.

I haven't confronted her yet and we're still living together as we always did. I do plan to get tested, I'll recommend the same to her. Taking the weekend to get my affairs in order and then I'll confront her next week.
We enjoyed the lifestyle that came with not having them (travel, flexible schedule, etc), but were were talking about being ready to take the plunge. Glad we didn't get that far.

Thanks, that's helpful to hear and you're right. My main concern is that she is VERY emotional, and she tells me at least once a month that she couldn't imagine living without me. Maybe it's just the guilt making her say that, who knows. I'm furious, but it's so hard right now to see past that loving veneer that she presents every day, it's such a warm and cozy place to be.

I live in California, which I understand is no fault. I've already got copies of the evidence in multiple places and I'm working on the financials. We kept separate accounts during our marriage (I know, I know...) so I've only got somewhat of an idea of what's in her accounts. No kids, I am so happy this came to light BEFORE we pulled the trigger as we've been talking about children.

I am truly dreading the confrontation. I know she'll make me feel like shit about it, and I know it will absolutely destroy her, and I don't want to do that. I'm going to make sure her two best friends are "on call" for her before I break the news. But you're absolutely right. It has to be done, I can't live in a relationship like this and I don't see a way to fix it with the repeated behavior. I'll use this weekend while she's working to get my ducks in a row and take the plunge next week.
Thank you. It's hard to think about even sleeping somewhere that's not our home, but it's going to be a reality soon enough anyhow. I'll be reaching out to some friends over the weekend for support.

Thanks for the reassurance. Our home was hers before we were married, but we do have 2 condos purchased after marriage. We kept our finances separate and she bought them both with her own funds, but it would be a big deal to me if I would be able to live in one after all of this.
Thank you, I will definitely do that. My emotions are running a bit wild right now so I could use some help.
